locator: pp.3–12 p.9 (Comments on the Causal Argument for Physicalism), premise 3 (no universal overdetermination), read distributively
interpretation: Reading A of "The physical effects of mental causes are not all overdetermined": per mental cause. This is the reading under which a universal conclusion in identity-or-realization form follows (physicalistFork), and he says the argument "seems pretty clearly valid" (p.10). The sentence does not itself fix this scope, so it is a reading of the premise, not his stated quantifier. The clause "with a physical effect" is added so that the reading is independent of premise 2, matching his treating them as separate exits. Overdetermination as a distinct cause is his contrast at p.10; "or realized by" follows his generous conclusion at p.11.
